title: 凉州词
author: 王翰
intro: Grape wine in jade cups, a pipa playing on horseback — soldiers on the frontier drink before battle. “Don’t laugh if I lie drunk on the battlefield: since ancient times, how many came home?”
analysis: 这是一首写边塞军中宴饮的诗。凉州在今天甘肃武威，是唐代西北边疆的重镇。第一句全是名词：葡萄酒、夜光杯，都是西域来的稀罕东西，一下子就有了异域风情和热闹的气氛。第二句写正要喝酒，马上弹起了琵琶——“催”可以理解为催人喝酒，也可以理解为催人出发上战场。后两句是士兵的话：“我要是喝醉了躺在沙场上，你可别笑我；从古到今出去打仗的，有几个人能活着回来？”这话听起来豪爽洒脱，其实藏着很深的悲凉：正因为明天可能回不来，今天才要痛快地喝。用豪放的语气写悲伤，让这首诗格外动人。另外，王之涣也写过一首有名的《凉州词》（“黄河远上白云间”），“凉州词”是当时流行的曲调名，很多诗人都用它写边塞诗。
analysisEn: Liangzhou (today’s Wuwei in Gansu) was a key garrison town on the Tang dynasty’s northwest frontier, on the road to Central Asia. The first line is just a list of beautiful things: grape wine and “night-glowing cups” of fine jade — both exotic luxuries from the Western Regions. In seven characters we are at a lively frontier feast. In the second line, just as the soldiers lift their cups, someone plays the pipa on horseback. The word 催 (“to urge, hurry”) can be read two ways: the music urges them to drink up, or it urges them to ride out to battle. Both readings work, and the tension between them matters. The last two lines are a soldier talking: “If I lie drunk on the battlefield, don’t laugh at me. Since ancient times, how many men who went to war ever came back?” On the surface this is bold and carefree. Underneath it is deeply sad: they drink so hard tonight precisely because they may die tomorrow. Saying something tragic in a light, swaggering voice is what makes the poem unforgettable. Note that “Song of Liangzhou” was the name of a popular tune; many poets wrote words for it. The other famous one is Wang Zhihuan’s, which begins “The Yellow River climbs far up among white clouds” — don’t mix the two up.
background: Wang Han (687?–726?) was a Tang official known for his bold, extravagant personality and love of horses and music. Few of his poems survive; this one is by far the best known.
pronunciation: “几人回”的“几”读 jǐ。“琵琶”读 pí pá（第二个字常读轻声，这里按本调标）。其余无特殊读音。
version: 采用统编小学语文教材版本，原题《凉州词二首》其一。“凉州词”是唐代乐府曲调名，王之涣、张籍等也有同题作品。

lines.py: pú táo měi jiǔ yè guāng bēi
lines.en: Sweet grape wine in cups of glowing jade —

lines.py: yù yǐn pí pá mǎ shàng cuī
lines.lit: about to drink, the pipa on horseback urges.
lines.en: we lift them, and a pipa on horseback calls us on.

lines.py: zuì wò shā chǎng jūn mò xiào
lines.lit: Lying drunk on the battlefield — sir, do not laugh;
lines.en: If I fall drunk on the battlefield, don’t laugh at me:

lines.py: gǔ lái zhēng zhàn jǐ rén huí
lines.lit: since ancient times, of those who went to war, how many returned?
lines.en: since time began, how many soldiers ever made it home?

words.en: Liangzhou, a frontier town (today’s Wuwei, Gansu)
song lyrics (here: words to a tune)
words.note: 这里指配曲演唱的歌词，不是宋词的“词”。
汉代从西域传入，现代汉语常用词。
传说夜里能发光的玉杯，今天甘肃酒泉仍出产。

words.en: to be about to; to want to
words.note: 现代汉语“欲望”“摇摇欲坠”。
从西域传入的乐器，今天仍常见。
古义“在马背上”；现代汉语“马上”是“立刻”的意思。

words.en: to go to war; military campaigns
words.note: 现代汉语也用，如“南征北战”。

imagery.name: 酒
imagery.zh: 美酒是边塞宴会的热闹，也是士兵面对死亡时的放纵与豁达。
imagery.en: Wine is the cheer of the frontier feast — and the soldiers’ way of facing death with a careless smile.

imagery.name: 琵琶
imagery.zh: 西域传来的琵琶在马上弹奏，带来异域风情，也像在催人出征。
imagery.en: A pipa from Central Asia played on horseback gives the scene its frontier flavour — and sounds like a call to ride out.

imagery.name: 马
imagery.zh: “马上”提醒我们：这是随时要上战场的军营，酒宴随时会结束。
imagery.en: “On horseback” reminds us this is an army camp: the feast could end at any moment for battle.
